page.overview:
What is Spring Bonnie?

Spring Bonnie is a spring lock suit created by Henry Emily and primarily worn by William Afton. He was used in Fredbear's Family Diner alongside the diner's mascot Fredbear until the restaurant's closure after William used the suit to abduct and kill one of Henry's children. Spring Bonnie would continue to be favored by William and used in his numerous murders until he himself would be killed by the spring locks in the suit, although his death wouldn't last.

Spring Bonnie is a patchwork, ragged yellowish-brown rabbit with a face similar to Bonnie’s, just with yellow fur. He also has lifeless eyes and two rows of horrid and yellow smiling teeth. When William puts the Spring Bonnie costume back on ten years later, it is musty and peeling at the edges of the mouth. The giant, absurd-looking rabbit costume also has big, matted paws and two gaping holes for eyes that are dark and hollow.

In the graphic novel rendition, Spring Bonnie is nearly identical to Bonnie, with gold fur and a red bowtie on his chest.

Spring Bonnie was an animatronic performer at Fredbear's Family Diner, a small diner in New Harmony, Utah owned by Henry Emily and William Afton. The costumes at the diner were designed to both be worn by others and be used as working animatronics, with mechanisms called spring locks holding back all of the animatronic parts. William typically wore the Spring Bonnie costume, dancing and miming along with songs for guests. On Halloween of 1983, however, William put on the suit and made his way to a closet where Henry's children Charlotte and Sammy were sleeping. He looked at the two for a bit before grabbing one of them and taking them away to kill them. This would lead to the diner's closure.
